chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

An unmarried woman was brought to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him), and they claimed that she had committed adultery. So he ordered the women to look at her, and they said, 'She is a virgin.' So he said, 'I would not whip one upon whom is a seal from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.' And he (peace be upon him) used to accept the testimony of women in cases similar to this.
ai.seo_question: How did Imam Ali (peace be upon him) use women's testimony to determine virginity for legal punishment?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights Imam Ali’s (peace be upon him) pragmatic application of *shahadat al-nisa* (testimony of women) in personal status matters, specifically regarding virginity. By linking the physical 'seal' (*khatam*) to divine signification, he established a precedent where women’s testimony suffices to prevent the hadd punishment of flogging, illustrating the flexibility of Shia jurisprudence in evidentiary standards.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘They came to Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> with an unmarried woman alleging that she had committed adultery. So he<sup>asws</sup> ordered the women to look at her, so they said, ‘She is a virgin’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> would not be the one to whip one upon whom is a seal from Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic’. And he<sup>asws</sup> used to allow the testimony of the women in (cases) similar to this’.
en.sarwar: 9. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Muhammad ibn al-Hassan Shammun from ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Abd al- Rahman from Misma‘ ibn ‘ Abd al-Malik who has narrated the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that ’Amir al-Mu’minin, Ali, Alayhi al-Salam, in the case of an atheist would issue a judgment.

If two just and acceptable people testified against him and one thousand in his favor, he (the Imam) would accept the testimony of two people. He (the Imam) would reject the testimony of one thousand because it is a hidden religion.” (It is considered applicable when the testimonies are presented in different times.)
